role.title: SVP Manufacturing
role.description:
**Position Summary**

The Senior Vice President, Manufacturing is the enterprise leader responsible for the strategy, performance, scalability, and continuous improvement of Mama’s Creations’ manufacturing network.

This executive owns the development and execution of an enterprise manufacturing strategy that enables profitable growth while delivering uncompromising safety, food safety, Grandma Quality, service, cost, capacity, and operational performance. The SVP will ensure Mama’s manufacturing capabilities evolve ahead of the Company’s growth, customer requirements, innovation pipeline, and acquisition strategy.

The role builds on Mama’s established “One Factory, Three Locations” operating model, creating common operating systems, performance standards, management routines, capabilities, and accountability across the manufacturing network located in NY/NJ.

The SVP Manufacturing will be a key member of the senior leadership team and a strategic partner to Operations, Supply Chain, FSQA, Engineering, Finance, People Operations, Culinary/R&D, Commercial, and other functions.

Base Pay: $250,000 - $300,000; Bonus Target: 40%; LTI Eligible

**Key Responsibilities**

Enterprise Manufacturing Strategy

* Develop and execute Mama’s multi-year manufacturing strategy aligned with the Company’s growth, profitability, innovation, and customer strategies.
* Translate the corporate strategy into clear manufacturing priorities, capabilities, capacity requirements, technology investments, and operating plans.
* Establish the roadmap for an increasingly integrated Mama’s manufacturing network, advancing the One Factory, Three Locations model.
* Determine when capacity should be created through existing facilities, expansion, automation, new facilities, acquisitions, or external manufacturing.
* Anticipate future production requirements and ensure that manufacturing capacity, capabilities, infrastructure, and talent are positioned ahead of demand.
* Regularly assess manufacturing footprint, capacity utilization, constraints, and investment requirements.
* This enterprise orientation is consistent with current external SVP benchmarks, which distinguish the SVP level through manufacturing strategy and footprint optimization rather than simply managing current production.

Manufacturing Performance & Operational Excellence

* Establish a consistent manufacturing operating system with common KPIs, operating reviews, accountability mechanisms, and problem-solving disciplines.
* Drive measurable, sustainable improvement across facilities using Lean manufacturing, structured problem-solving, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Identify performance gaps and ensure corrective actions produce durable results rather than short-term fixes.
* Promote sharing of best practices across all manufacturing locations.
* Comparable manufacturing executives are expected to lead continuous process improvement, line efficiency, cost reduction, KPI management, benchmarking, technology adoption, and operational excellence.

Safety, Food Safety & Grandma Quality

* Establish a manufacturing culture where employee safety and food safety are non-negotiable.
* Ensure manufacturing processes consistently deliver Mama’s commitment to Grandma Quality.
* Partner closely with FSQA leadership to maintain compliance with applicable FDA, USDA, FSMA, HACCP, GMP and customer requirements.
* Ensure manufacturing leaders maintain sustained audit readiness and promptly address corrective and preventive actions.
* Ensure productivity improvements never compromise employee safety, food safety, product integrity, or customer requirements.
* Mama’s internal manufacturing leadership model already places food safety, regulatory compliance, audit readiness and Grandma Quality at the center of plant accountability.

Capacity, Capital & Automation Strategy

* Own the long-range manufacturing capacity plan.
* Develop and prioritize the enterprise manufacturing capital roadmap in partnership with Finance, Engineering, Reliability, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders.
* Establish rigorous business cases for capital investments based on capacity, productivity, safety, quality, reliability, labor reduction, growth, and ROI.
* Lead major facility expansions, production line additions, equipment installations, and manufacturing technology investments.
* Evaluate automation opportunities that improve capacity, consistency, employee safety, labor productivity, quality, and scalability.
* Ensure capital projects deliver intended financial and operational benefits following implementation.

Financial & P&L Leadership

* Own enterprise manufacturing budgets and overall manufacturing cost performance.
* Establish annual productivity and cost-improvement objectives across the network.
* Partner with Finance to understand manufacturing cost drivers and identify sustainable margin-improvement opportunities.
* Drive disciplined management of labor, overtime, yield, waste, downtime, supplies, maintenance, and other controllable manufacturing expenses.
* Ensure plant leaders understand the financial impact of operating decisions.
* Balance cost and productivity objectives with safety, service, Grandma Quality, employee capability, and long-term operational health.
* External benchmarks similarly position manufacturing VPs/SVPs as responsible for budgets, capacity, workforce requirements, cost control, quality and resource planning.

Manufacturing Organization & Leadership Development

* Build a high-performing manufacturing leadership organization capable of supporting Mama’s continued growth.
* Lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable senior manufacturing and plant leaders.
* Establish clear decision rights and accountability between enterprise manufacturing leadership and individual facilities.
* Build succession plans for critical manufacturing leadership positions.
* Partner with People Operations on organizational design, workforce planning, leadership development, performance management, employee engagement, and succession.
* Establish leadership expectations that reinforce accountability while maintaining Mama’s values and culture.
* Develop an internal pipeline of future Plant Directors, VPs, and manufacturing executives.

Workforce & Labor Strategy

* Establish the enterprise manufacturing workforce strategy in partnership with People Operations.
* Develop scalable labor models tied to production volumes, product mix, line capabilities, and operating schedules.
* Create greater consistency across plants in labor planning, overtime management, staffing models, skills development, and workforce utilization.
* Champion frontline leadership capability and supervisor development.
* Support strategies that improve attendance, retention, workforce stability, productivity, and employee engagement.
* Evaluate opportunities to reduce dependence on temporary labor and excessive overtime through improved workforce planning, scheduling, automation, and retention.

Reliability, Engineering & Technology

* Partner with Engineering and Reliability leadership to build preventive and predictive maintenance capabilities.

* Executive-level communication and influencing abilities.
* Bilingual English/Spanish capability beneficial.

role.title: Director of ITAD Operations
role.description:
**Director of ITAD Operations**

 

**A Candid Look at Our Culture**

Dynamic is a high-accountability, low-ego workplace. We take our work and commitments seriously, but we don't take ourselves too seriously.

At **Dynamic Lifecycle Innovations**, we give electronics their next best life while protecting our planet and our customers' interests. As a Certified Great Place to Work® since 2017, we've built a team culture that's rewarding, engaging, and FUN! But don't just take our word for it—see what our Team Members have to say.

**How We Hire: The Head, Heart, and Briefcase**

We believe great performance comes from alignment across three areas:

* **Head** – your natural behavioral drives and cognitive agility (measured by our Predictive Index assessment)
* ❤️**Heart** – your values, passions, and what drives you to make a meaningful impact
* **Briefcase** – your experiences, skills, and results from past roles

Every step of our process is designed to understand you in all three areas. It's how we ensure the best mutual fit, not just for what you can do, but for how you'll thrive here long-term.

**\*\*Required Step** **- You'll start with the Predictive Index (PI) assessment** (takes <20 minutes total), then move through structured interviews, work samples, and culture-focused interviews. We respect your time and promise clear, timely communication throughout.

**Location:** Onsite within our Onalaska, WI, or Hendersonville, TN facilities.

**Total Cash Compensation (Base + Bi-Annual Incentive):** $170,000 - $250,000

**Benefits Include:**

* Comprehensive health benefits starting the first of the month following hire
* 401(k) with company match
* Quarterly incentive opportunity
* Generous paid time off and paid holidays

**Your Purpose**

As the Director of ITAD Operations, you'll lead the people and operations that give technology its next best life. Our IT asset disposition (ITAD) facilities operate much like manufacturing environments, where production flow, labor planning, equipment, inventory, quality, and safety all contribute to performance. If you've led manufacturing operations and enjoy developing people while improving how work gets done, your experience could make a significant impact here.

Reporting to the Executive Vice President of ITAD, you'll turn strategy into results across Dynamic's primary and satellite facilities. You'll develop leaders, strengthen operational consistency, and use data and technology to improve efficiency, profitability, and customer satisfaction.

This is an opportunity to shape how our operations grow. From improving processes on the floor to building the capabilities needed across multiple locations, your leadership will help Dynamic process IT assets securely, efficiently, and profitably while advancing our mission.

**What You'll Do**

* **Lead operations across multiple facilities.** Turn business priorities into clear operating plans, align leaders around shared goals, and drive consistent execution across primary and satellite locations.
* **Develop leaders who develop their teams.** Coach, mentor, and empower your leaders to build team capability, own results, and prepare future leaders through training and succession planning.
* **Improve production flow and performance.** Apply Lean manufacturing practices, Gemba walks, and root cause analysis to remove bottlenecks, reduce waste, and improve productivity and quality.
* **Make performance visible and actionable.** Build dashboards and scorecards that help teams understand results, recognize issues early, and take ownership of improvement.
* **Connect operational decisions to profitability.** Manage labor, costs, and budgets while aligning production schedules and capacity with business demand and customer commitments.
* **Use technology to improve how work gets done.** Partner across teams to strengthen ERP use, inventory management, and process automation as operations grow.
* **Protect our people and our customers' trust.** Hold high standards for safety, quality, environmental compliance, and data security while ensuring customer assets are handled securely, and service commitments are met.

**What You Bring (Briefcase)**

* Bachelor's degree in operations management, business administration, engineering, supply chain management, or a related field. Additional relevant experience will be considered in lieu of formal education.
* Eight or more years of progressive operations leadership experience, including significant experience managing teams and operational performance. Demonstrated success leading complex, high-volume processing, manufacturing, reverse logistics, refurbishment, or ITAD operations.
* Experience leading operational teams across multiple facilities and developing leaders who deliver consistent results.
* Demonstrated success improving operational performance through continuous improvement, financial discipline, and data-informed decisions.
* Preferred: MBA
* Preferred: Knowledge of IT asset disposition, secondary markets for IT equipment and components, and the processing requirements of servers, networking equipment, storage systems, and GPUs.
* Preferred: Familiarity with R2, e-Stewards, NAID AAA, and ISO standards, along with ITAD data security and environmental compliance requirements.
* Preferred: Knowledge of Lean Six Sigma, Total Quality Management, or the Toyota Production System.

**Skills & Abilities (Head)**

* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement practices, including Kaizen, 5S, Gemba walks, and root cause analysis.
* Financial acumen connecting operational decisions to gross margin, operating expenses, and overall profitability.
* Understanding of forecasting, labor and capacity planning, and Sales & Operations Planning.
* Ability to use ERP systems, inventory management technology, production planning, and automation to improve operations.
* Analytical skills to build actionable dashboards and scorecards that make performance visible in real time.
* Clear communication, active listening, and project management skills that help teams align and execute.
* Leadership skills in coaching, mentoring, training, delegation, and succession planning.

**❤️** **Who You Are (Heart)**

You're a leader who connects strategy with what happens on the floor. You set clear expectations, listen closely, and help people understand how their work contributes to the bigger picture. You're comfortable digging into the data, asking thoughtful questions, and working alongside your teams to solve problems.

You hold high standards for results and how they're achieved. You build accountability through trust, develop leaders who can own their decisions, and look for better ways to work without losing sight of safety, quality, or the customer. You bring the judgment to balance today's operational demands with the capabilities Dynamic needs for its next stage of growth.

**Why You'll Love Working Here**

**Purpose with Impact:** Help give electronics their "next best life" while protecting the planet 
 **Award-Winning Culture:** We put people first as a Certified Great Place to Work® since 2017 
**Executive Influence:** Shape long-term enterprise strategy with your executive peers

**Transform at Scale:** Lead the modernization of technology, data, and AI through growth
 **Build Something Lasting:** Dynamic is privately owned without PE – our focus is long-term, sustainable growth, and you'll help us build a foundation to enable decades of success

* **️** **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Dynamic Lifecycle Innovations is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing fair employment opportunities for all based on merit. For positions subject to state contract requirements, we adhere to state affirmative action obligations and take proactive steps to ensure equal opportunity in our hiring practices. We do not discriminate or make any employment decisions on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

role.title: Director, Operations
role.description:
**Company Description**

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country’s largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

 **Job Description**

**Position Purpose:**

Reporting to and assisting the Veolia Water New York, Inc. Vice President of Operations , this position is responsible for the overall management of the Production and Transmission and Distribution System (T&D) for Veolia Water Westchester, Inc. (VWWC). This individual will provide managerial oversight to the operations, maintenance and construction activities in the Production and the Transmission and Distribution (T&D) Departments to ensure the following objectives are met: departmental financials as they relate to both the budget and approved rate of returns, regulatory compliance, safety, employee development, customer experience, and continuous improvement. This individual is also responsible for managing external relations with municipal and community leaders.

* Revenue - $70 M
* Annual Budget - $32 M
* Capital Budget - $30 M
* Customers – 48,000
* Population Served – 200,000
* Direct Reports – 2 (Manager of Production and Superintendent of T&D)
* Indirect Reports – 62 (non-exempt, non-bargaining and bargaining)
* Budget Accountabilities

**Primary Duties/Responsibilities:**

* Support the Vice President of Operations of the NY Division by developing policy and strategies for VWWC, specifically non-revenue water and asset management.
* Provide direction and management to ensure that VWWC operates in compliance with updated management practices, with data and record retention for auditable trails. Ensure all staff follows Veolia policies and manuals.
* Direct all the statutory and regulatory requirements for health and safety to provide a safe and efficient place of work for our employees. Assist theVice President of the NY Division in providing customers with safe, reliable and adequate service in the most cost effective way.
* Maintain compliance with all company, governmental and/or environmental regulations and policies to provide safe potable water.
* Direct the collection of sufficient data to manage risk and make effective management decisions.
* Conduct appropriate performance reviews to drive results and demonstrate continuous improvement in water treatment, water transmission, construction and distribution.
* Participate in the preparation of accurate and realistic annual operating and capital plans. Monitor Key Performance Indicators.
* Assists in the control of operating and capital expenditures pursuant to the time and monetary schedules contained in the plans.
* Review and analyze non-revenue water statistics, determine appropriate plans and implement agreed recommendations.
* Directs the operations team to ensure the attainment of service, financial goals and major program efforts.
* Ensures the training and cross training of employees through on the job training workshops or schools, evaluation or appraisals, to equip them to perform their assigned duties efficiently and effectively.
* Oversee laboratory process including sampling and testing.
* Assist in employee and career development programs, through ongoing education, seminars and in-house training.
* Participate in labor relations issues including negotiations, grievance, and arbitrations.
* Work with the Regional President of the NY Division with respect to community relations by attending meetings with mayors and town administrators.
* Conduct special studies or analysis as requested by the Vice President of Operations of the NY Division.
* Oversees the Company's fleet maintenance and fleet leasing program.
* May provide testimony in liability and litigation cases.
* Responsible for documenting, developing and maintaining Company's "Emergency Response Plan".
* Keep current with Federal, State and local health regulations.
* Assist with rate case filing including data collection, interrogatories, and testimony.
* Advise, direct and recommend work plan for the long-term main replacement program.
* Direct water treatment, water transmission, construction/distribution related budget items.
* Direct all personnel in stations to ensure proper operating procedures are maintained.
* Ensure timely response to customer water quality inquiries and complaints.
* Direct SCADA operation.
* Participate in the due-diligence process for new business ventures. Includes operations, workforce plans, and customer service. Support, direct, assume responsibility as required for integration of new operations into the NY Division portfolio.

**Work Environment:**

* Office environment.

 
**Qualifications**

**Education/Experience/Background:**

* BS degree in engineering, business administration, or other management is desired or equivalent work experience.
* 7 – 10 years of experience with at least five (5) years experience in a supervisory role.
* Experience in various phases of utility operations, construction, engineering and customer service.
* Thorough understanding of water utility construction and water treatment.
* Experience in a unionized work environment is preferable.
* Knowledge of water treatment methods, distribution system operations and maintenance, Utility accounting systems and procedures.

**Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:**

* Proficient Computer Skills including MS Office Suite.
* Excellent Communications Skills both verbal and written. Ability to communicate clearly.
* Excellent Leadership Skills including decision making and planning skills.
* Excellent managerial and supervisory abilities, effective negotiating.
* Organizational Skills.
* Project Management Skills.
* Interpersonal Skills.
* Performance management.
* Required to work under pressure and work on stand-by (24 hr stand-by approximately every 5 weeks).

**Physical Requirements:**

* Must be able to sit at a computer for long periods of time.

 
**Additional Information**

**Pay Range:** $145000 to $160000 Per Year.

**Benefits:** Veolia’s comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

Disclaimer: The salary, other compensation, and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, subject to applicable law.

role.title: Director, Manufacturing Operations FP&A
role.description:
When you work at Trex, you’re helping to grow and enhance a true original. You join a company that boldly launched an entire industry… and still leads the way.

As Director, Manufacturing Operations FP&A, you will lead the financial planning, analysis, and decision-support for operational excellence, procurement, and logistics. This role establishes the operating-finance framework, translates operational drivers into financial outcomes, and provides forward-looking insight to improve cost competitiveness, capacity utilization, service, working capital, and capital allocation. The Director serves as a strategic partner to plant, supply chain, procurement, logistics, engineering, finance, and corporate leadership; owns the integrity and consistency of operational forecasts and KPIs; and drives accountability for performance and corrective actions across the network.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Put safety first – Always!
* Lead and foster our “people first” culture.
* Forecasting & Planning
 + Support monthly, quarterly, and annual forecasting for manufacturing, procurement, and logistics, including volume, material costs, inbound and outbound freight, warehousing, and distribution costs.
 + Establish and govern driver-based models that project operational and financial performance under multiple demand, production, sourcing, commodity, freight, and capacity scenarios.
 + Direct the cross-functional planning process with operations, engineering, procurement, logistics, and supply chain leaders to validate assumptions, reconcile operational plans, and align forecast inputs.
 + Own the annual operating plan and long-range financial planning processes for the manufacturing network, including productivity roadmaps, capacity requirements, sourcing strategies, logistics costs, and capital needs.
 + Prepare bridge analyses that clearly explain financial forecast-to-forecast and forecast-to-plan variances.
 + Develop executive-level scenarios and recommendations that quantify trade-offs among cost, capacity, inventory, customer service, sourcing risk, and capital deployment.
 + Define planning standards, calendars, assumptions, and review routines to improve forecast accuracy and accountability across functions and locations.
* Operational & Financial Analysis
 + Analyze actual manufacturing results including productivity, material usage, downtime, labor efficiency, machine utilization, and OEE.
 + Deliver monthly financial KPI reporting packages with clear commentary and recommendations.
 + Perform variance analysis on production costs, inventory, and plant performance.
 + Investigate root causes of unfavorable trends and partner on corrective actions.
 + Monitor and analyze inventory accuracy, production variances, waste, and yield.
 + Evaluate cost impacts of engineering changes, process improvements, and capital projects.
* Procurement & Logistics FP&A
 + Lead financial planning and performance analysis for direct and indirect procurement, inbound and outbound logistics, warehousing, distribution, and third-party service providers.
 + Partner with procurement to evaluate supplier negotiations, sourcing events, make-versus-buy decisions, contract economics, commodity exposure, purchase price variance, and total cost of ownership.
 + Partner with logistics and operations to analyze freight rates, mode and carrier mix, fuel and accessorial charges, network design, warehouse productivity, inventory positioning, detention, demurrage, and service-level trade-offs.
 + Build savings and productivity governance that validates baselines, timing, one-time costs, risk adjustments, and realized P&L and cash-flow benefits.
 + Provide financial support for supplier and carrier scorecards, procurement pipelines, logistics bids, and network-optimization initiatives.
 + Assess working-capital implications of sourcing and logistics decisions, including payment terms, order quantities, lead times, safety stock, inventory turns, and obsolescence risk.
* Leadership & Business Partnership
 + Serve as the senior finance advisor to manufacturing, procurement, logistics, and corporate leadership, shaping decisions and constructively challenging operating assumptions.
 + Present concise, decision-oriented insights and recommendations to executive leadership, including risks, opportunities, sensitivities, and required actions.
 + Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing FP&A team; set priorities, establish performance expectations, provide coaching, and build succession and analytical capabilities.
 + Build strong relationships across operations, engineering, procurement, logistics, supply chain, accounting, treasury, and finance while maintaining clear ownership and accountability.
 + Create and maintain standardized KPI definitions, reporting governance, and management review routines across the manufacturing and supply chain network.
 + Sponsor process, data, and systems improvements that increase forecast quality, analytical speed, scalability, and decision usefulness.
 + Influence cross-functional leaders without direct authority and ensure agreed actions are assigned, measured, and completed.
* Other duties as assigned

 

**JOB LOCATION**

Winchester, Virginia, United States

 

**POSITION TYPE**

Full-Time/Regular

 

**EXPERIENCE**

We are looking for leaders with a Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Supply Chain, or related field and 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing finance, FP&A, supply chain finance, procurement finance, logistics finance, or plant controllership.

* Required Skills & Experience
 + Experience leading complex cross-functional planning and decision-support processes.
 + Demonstrated experience leading forecasting, operational modeling, variance analysis, annual planning, long-range planning, and executive decision support in a multi-site environment.
 + Prior people-leadership experience, including developing finance talent and leading through influence across operational functions.
 + Executive-level analytical judgment with the ability to synthesize complex operational and financial information into clear decisions and actions.
 + Expert in Excel, data modeling, and reporting tools (OneStream).
 + Experience with ERP systems (JD Edwards).
 + Executive-level communication and presentation skills, with demonstrated ability to influence senior operational and financial leaders.
 + Ability to lead enterprise process improvements, establish governance, manage competing priorities, and deliver results through cross-functional teams.
* Preferred Skills & Experience
 + Multi-site manufacturing experience
 + MBA, CPA, CMA, or other relevant advanced degree or professional certification

At Trex, we believe in persevering even when there’s no road map, embracing groundbreaking as a way of life. We encourage multiple perspectives and welcome diverse people who problem-solve, adapt, and innovate – always with a firm foundation in safety and integrity.

 

**SALARY**

Base Salary Range: $163,000 - $210,000 annually

The salary range provided serves as a general guideline for potential compensation for this position. It reflects the base salary and does not account for other benefits or additional compensation opportunities that may apply. This role is also eligible for further compensation through an annual/sales bonus, in addition to the base salary.

At Trex, individual base salaries are determined based on various factors, including relevant skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location. We are committed to maintaining pay equity and considering the internal equity of our existing team members when finalizing compensation offers. In addition to competitive pay, Trex offers a comprehensive benefits package, which is detailed below.

 

**BENEFITS & PERKS**

We believe that real effort should be rewarded. We take care of you as part of our Trex family so you can take care of yours. Here are some of the perks beyond the paycheck:

* **Time Off:** We’ll give you paid holidays and paid vacation.
* **Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance:** Choose from a variety of options. We’ll cover a generous share of the cost. Plus, you can earn lower rates through our wellness program.
* **401(k) With Company Match:** Save for your retirement and we’ll match it dollar for dollar.
* **Tuition Reimbursement:** We’re all about lifting each other to the next level. When you’re ready to get the degree, we’ll pick up part of the tab.
* **Training and Education:** We offer dozens of options to boost your performance – both online and on-site nearby.
* **Stock Purchase Program:** Invest in Trex at a discounted price.
* **Employee Discount Program:** When you make the World’s No. 1 Decking Brand, you’ll probably want to enjoy the finished product yourself. We’ll give you a discount.

 

**WHO WE ARE**

Over 30 years ago, our founders created the world’s first high-performance, low-maintenance composite decking and outdoor living products. That entrepreneurial spirit still drives us today as we continue to redefine our industry and lead the way for what’s next in outdoor living. Today, Trex is the world’s #1 brand of sustainability-made, wood-alternative decking, and deck railing – all proudly manufactured in the USA. As a publicly traded company [NYSE: TREX], we take pride in being the largest recycler of plastic film in the country as well as caring for the communities and the planet where we live. We nurture meaningful connections, from local engagement and investment to eco-friendly products and sustainable manufacturing processes.

Everything we do is grounded in our values and guided by our beliefs. We are looking for candidates who embody our core values:

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
Dairy Farmers of America (DFA), a dairy marketing cooperative owned by more than 12,500 family farmers. Our mark matters and it represents the wholesomeness of dairy that we share with our communities and loved ones. DFA manufactures a variety of dairy products, including cheese, butter, fluid milk, ice cream, dairy ingredients and more, under well-known and established regional brands. Our fingerprints touch thousands of brands across the marketplace, and we're passionate about delivering the simple pleasures of dairy to people everywhere, straight from our family farm-owners. We are proud to provide families with fresh delicious dairy products.

By joining DFA, you can help us continue to make a difference that matters. We care deeply about the well-being of our neighbors and friends, and we celebrate the diversity of our company and our world. It takes an incredible team to deliver the goodness of dairy and enrich our communities – come join us!

**GENERAL PURPOSE**

Direct and coordinate overall plant operations and priorities, and through managers, supervisors, and staff, ensure product is produced efficiently and within cost parameters. Provide work direction to management and employees within the guidelines of standard work rules, union contract provisions (if applicable), and employment policies. Is held accountable for achieving the plant's key performance indicators. Support the Continuous Improvement (CI) initiative to improve productivity, quality, efficiency of operations, and the facility's culture. Manage the overall operating budget including capital and expense projects. Direct personnel activities of department, such as recruitment, hiring, performance evaluations, and salary adjustments using independent judgment within the framework of established human resources policies and practices.

This plant manager job is a single incumbent role responsible for multiple plants or a large and/or complex plant that may also have an assistant plant manager(s) within the plant.

**JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Manage plant operations in all areas of responsibility including administration, production, processing, packaging, quality, maintenance, warehousing, shipping, purchasing, safety, and environmental

* Establish production priorities to ensure product is produced efficiently and within cost parameters while maintaining safety, quality and sanitation standards; obtain optimum production and utilization of workforce, machines, and equipment

* Review and analyze production, quality control, maintenance, and operational reports to ensure compliance and determine causes of non-conformity with product specifications, customer requirements, FDA/government regulations, etc. Report any non-compliance immediately per established protocol

* Analyze plant operations to ensure that the facility maintains a leadership position in the industry and that it takes advantage of new processes and technologies that become available

* Interact with customers to meet their expectations on a variety of goals including operational, customer service, financial, and quality

* Develop, monitor, and drive plant key performance indicators (KPI's) related to safety, quality, productivity and finances. Strive for continuous improvement in KPI results. Promote continuous improvement culture and activities

* Understand plant P&L to drive plant performance; participate in the development of annual operating, capital and expense budgets; provide reliable and accurate information to finance to meet end-of-month closing schedules

* Manage or oversee all corporate, customer, and government audits to ensure compliance

* Conduct meetings with management and staff to ensure all operational issues are being communicated and addressed expediently with a common understanding of goals

* Communicate company goals and assist in establishing objectives that align with plant and company goals; communicate plant direction, focus and goals

* Provide appropriate direction, mentoring, training, and development planning for managers. Identify and retain highly effective personnel through proper selection, training and task assignment. Actively work with direct reports to cultivate capabilities and utilize strengths to support career development and succession planning efforts

* Maintain safe working conditions for employees and compliance with all company, state and federal regulations regarding health and safety issues

* Follow all DFA good manufacturing practices (GMP) and work in a manner consistent with all company regulatory, food safety, quality, and sanitation requirements

* The requirements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employee, but is not a complete list of responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Other duties may be assigned as required

**BENEFITS:**

* Health and Welfare benefits begin 1st of the month after start date
* 401(k) with company contribution – 100% vested at day one of eligibility
* Competitive pay
* Paid vacation and holidays
* Career growth opportunities – we promote from within!
* Comprehensive healthcare benefits
* Service recognition and employee rewards
* Employee referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Work for dairy farm families

Requirements:

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

* High school diploma or equivalent

* Undergraduate degree in related curriculum preferred

* 8 or more years' experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably food and/or beverage manufacturing

* 2 or more years' management experience

* Proven track record of improved results in the areas of quality, safety, service and cost

* Certification and/or License – may be required during course of employment

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**

* Strong knowledge of manufacturing process flow and importance to process

* Strong knowledge of continuous improvement models

* Thorough understanding of regulatory laws and responsibilities as it relates to facility standards

* Proficient understanding of budgeting and cost control

• Skill in leadership and coaching; strong knowledge of principles and practices of supervision, training, and personnel management • Knowledge of and skill with Microsoft Office Suite and company computer systems

* Skill in critical thinking, analysis, mathematical calculations, and statistical evaluations

* Able to work in collaboration effectively and foster good teamwork

* Able to interact positively and work effectively with others (interpersonal skills)

* Able to think and use independent judgment in planning and organizing multiple tasks and information

* Able to demonstrate strong initiative

* Able to take appropriate steps to find solutions to problems

* Able to present options and ideas to current processes or procedures

* Able to handle challenging or conflict situations with tact and professionalism

* Able to communicate with various levels of personnel to ensure customers' needs and requirements are met

* Able to interpret and apply company policies

* Able to adapt and manage to change effectively

* Must be able to read, write and speak English

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**Plant Manager – Furniture Manufacturing**

**Position Summary**

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on, and results-driven **Plant Manager** to lead our furniture manufacturing operations. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced manufacturing leader to take ownership of plant performance, develop a strong leadership team, improve production processes, and make a direct impact on the success and growth of the facility.

The Plant Manager will oversee all aspects of plant operations, including production, safety, quality, scheduling, cost management, and employee development. This individual will provide leadership and oversight to department supervisors across the facility, ensuring all departments work together to achieve production, quality, safety, and operational goals.

The ideal candidate is a strong, people-focused leader with a solid manufacturing background who knows how to motivate teams, develop supervisors, improve processes, solve problems, and create a culture of accountability, teamwork, safety, and quality.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Plant Operations & Production**

* Direct and oversee daily manufacturing operations to ensure production goals, quality standards, and delivery expectations are consistently met.
* Coordinate activities across departments to maximize productivity, efficiency, and workflow.
* Identify and implement process improvements to reduce waste, control labor costs, and increase operational efficiency.
* Develop and monitor production goals, performance metrics, and operational procedures.
* Oversee equipment needs, maintenance coordination, and resource planning to support production demands.

**Leadership & Employee Development**

* Provide overall leadership, direction, and oversight to department supervisors across all areas of the manufacturing plant.
* Lead, coach, and develop supervisors to ensure effective management of their respective departments and teams.
* Establish clear performance expectations, goals, and accountability for department supervisors.
* Monitor departmental performance and work with supervisors to address challenges, improve productivity, and achieve production goals.
* Oversee employee training and development initiatives to build a skilled, productive workforce.
* Promote teamwork, communication, and collaboration between departments to ensure smooth and efficient plant operations.
* Foster a positive work environment focused on employee engagement, accountability, safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

**Cost Management & Financial Performance**

* Develop and manage plant budgets while maintaining effective cost controls.
* Identify opportunities to reduce labor and production costs without sacrificing quality or safety.
* Implement and maintain production cost tracking systems to evaluate manufacturing performance.
* Monitor labor utilization, productivity, and operating expenses to support profitability.

**Safety & Quality**

* Promote a safe working environment and ensure employees follow established safety procedures.
* Maintain high standards for product quality and accuracy throughout the manufacturing process.
* Monitor production processes and implement improvements to reduce defects, waste, and product returns.
* Ensure the facility has the necessary supplies, equipment, and resources to maintain safe and efficient operations.

**Systems & Process Improvement**

* Work closely with office personnel to improve administrative processes, reporting systems, and documentation.
* Establish and maintain effective production records and reporting procedures.
* Stay current with manufacturing technology, equipment, and industry best practices.
* Support improvements to systems and processes that enhance product quality, operational efficiency, and customer service.
* Perform other duties as needed to support the success of plant operations.

**Qualifications & Experience**

**Required Qualifications:**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Minimum of 5 years of manufacturing, production, scheduling, or operations experience.
* Minimum of 3 years of leadership or supervisory experience in a manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated ability to lead supervisors and teams, manage performance, and drive operational results.
* Strong problem-solving, organizational, communication, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* 5–7 years of manufacturing operations or production management experience.
* Previous Plant Manager, Operations Manager, Production Manager, or similar leadership experience.
* Experience in furniture manufacturing or a similar production environment.
* Experience managing multiple departments and supervising department leaders.
* Experience managing production costs, labor efficiency, budgets, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Bachelor's degree in Business, Manufacturing, Operations Management, or a related field is a plus, but equivalent hands-on experience will be considered.

**Key Skills & Competencies**

* Strong leadership and team-building skills.
* Employee development and performance management.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Strong time management and organizational abilities.
* Manufacturing and operational knowledge.
* Results-oriented mindset.
* Problem-solving and continuous improvement.
* Attention to detail and accountability.

**What We Offer**

We value our employees and offer a benefits package designed to support their health, financial well-being, and work-life balance.

* Health Insurance available after 90 days.
* 401(k) retirement plan available after one year.
* Paid vacation.
* Additional company benefits.

**Work Environment & Physical Requirements**

This position operates in a furniture manufacturing facility. The work environment may include exposure to airborne particles, fumes, moving mechanical equipment, vibration, and elevated noise levels.

The position requires frequent standing, walking, reaching, and use of hands. Occasional sitting, climbing, balancing, bending, kneeling, crouching, and crawling may be required.

The ability to regularly lift or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift or move up to 25 pounds is required. Specific vision requirements include close, distance, color, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

role.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
role.description:
The Howmet engines business produces world-class aerospace engine components, including investment castings, fasteners, rings and forgings. Our vacuum melted superalloys, machining, performance coatings and hot isostatic pressing for high performance parts enable the next generation of quieter, cleaner and more fuel-efficient aerospace engines. Able to supply more than 90% of structural and rotating aerospace engine components. 
 

Howmet Engines seeks an experienced professional to join our team! The **Continuous Improvement Director** at Howmet Aerospace is responsible for driving the implementation and sustained use of Lean principles, enhancing operational efficiency and fostering a culture of continuous improvement across the business segment This role serves as a teacher, coach and mentor, working closely with employees at all levels to build long-term adoption of CI practices. The Continuous Improvement Director partners with Senior Leadership to align improvement initiatives with business objectives, ensuring measurable impact on productivity, capacity and overall business segment performance.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Lead the continued development and enhancement of the Howmet Business System journey, including accelerating the Lean Execution Systems Assessment process and progress, working with plant teams on gap closure plans in support of advancing the CI culture across the business segment.
* Facilitate the Howmet Business System “HBS” journey best practice sharing within the location and across teams through a sustainable electronic system that allows users to search for common issues or problems.
* Lead OEE improvement actions deep dive with leaders and provide avenues for best practice sharing.
* Lead Howmet Business System implementation of continuous improvement initiatives and drive waste reductions utilizing Lean principles (JIT, Autonomation, Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen, 5S, Standard Work, Line/Cell Design, Single Piece Flow, Material Flow, Visual Management, SMED, TPM, Root Cause Problem Solving, etc.)
* Facilitate Hoshins, Kaizens, problem solving, and rapid improvement process events with internal personnel at all levels of the organization, consultants, customers, and suppliers as needed. This includes providing support to sustain all follow-throughs required to sustain the improvements initiated during those events, especially those concentrated on local improvement.
* Understand and analyze Profit and Loss (P&L) statements to identify opportunities for cost reduction, revenue enhancement, and margin improvement. Lead and collaborate with cross functional internal teams focused on shop floor factory improvements, which could include CAPEX.
* Assist team leaders in team skill and knowledge development to support meeting management goals, project management, improvements, results measurements, problem solving and related team skills.
* Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to track progress and measure the impact of improvement initiatives.
* Drive change management efforts to ensure successful implementation and sustainability of process improvements.
* Identify and share best practices, lessons learned, and success stories to promote knowledge sharing and continuous learning within the organization.
* Provide coaching and mentorship to team members across the organization to drive the Continuous Improvement mindset.
* May participate or lead other targeted initiatives or kaizens as directed by the BU, as defined by the Segment Vice President.
* Role may support other sites’ continuous improvement activities, as needed (e.g., training, project-based work, best practice support, etc.)

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Minimum 10 years of experience in manufacturing environments in areas such as: Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, or Operational Excellence
* Minimum of 7 years in leadership roles in Operations or Continuous Improvement
* Previous experience in an aerospace, automotive or other manufacturing environment requiring significant lean strategies to maintain wins and propel the organizations’ success through Continuous Improvement
* Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited institution
* Must be willing to travel up to 50% of the time, including domestic and international travel
* Strong working knowledge and understanding of Continuous Process Improvement methodologies such as Lean and Six Sigma.
* Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
* This position is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) which requires U.S. person status. ITAR defines U.S. person as an U.S. Citizen, U.S. Permanent Resident (i.e. 'Green Card Holder'), Political Asylee, or Refugee
* Employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s Degree and Master's Degree from an accredited institution in Engineering or Supply Chain field of study highly desired
* Project Management certification or earned certificate
* Experience developing operations leadership development programs in a manufacturing environment
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing improvement techniques, including hoshin, flow principles, Jidoka, Kanban, 5S, and “plan for every part” (PFEP).
* Strong skills in value stream mapping and associated improvement methodologies.
* Understanding of pillars of Toyota production system (JIT, Jidoka).
* Experience evaluating TAKT time vs. cycle time, determining work area constraints (i.e. cycle time constraint, periodic work constraints, downtime constraints).
* Experience on the shop floor, working with employees, and enhancing manufacturing processes.
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills require the ability to resolve conflicting interests and obtain cooperation.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills: able to develop and use structured approaches to identify root causes and recommend resolutions.
* Demonstrated experience in project leadership and project management skills, with ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously to meet objectives and key deadlines.

**Compensation and Benefits:**

If a pay range is identified for this job, it is based on a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. Actual compensation is subject to variation due to factors such as education, experience, skillset, market/business considerations, and/or location.

Howmet Aerospace offers a competitive benefits package to support the health, financial well-being, and professional growth of our employees. Benefits include:

* Comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision benefits coverage, including FSA and HSA account options
* Pre-tax and Roth 401(k) retirement savings plans offering employer matching funds and a separate employer retirement contribution
* Paid holidays and vacation time (eligibility, accrual, and usage are discretionary and governed by applicable policies)
* Paid parental leave and adoption assistance programs
* Life insurance and disability coverage plans
* Optional coverage plans for auto, home, legal, identity theft, and pet insurance
* Tuition Assistance Program and ongoing professional development opportunities
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

**Our Story:**

Howmet Aerospace Inc. (NYSE: HWM), headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, is a leading global provider of advanced engineered solutions for the aerospace and transportation industries. Our primary businesses focus on jet engine components, aerospace fastening systems, titanium structural parts and forged wheels. With $8.3 Billion in revenue in 2025, our products play a crucial role in enabling fuel efficiency and lightweighting, contributing to our customers’ success and making a positive impact on the world. To learn more about the way Howmet Aerospace Inc. is advancing the sustainability of our customers, markets, and communities where we operate, review the 2025 Environmental Social and Governance report at www.howmet.com/esg-report. Follow: LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube.

Howmet is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

role.title: Senior Manager, Performance and Quality
role.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

As the Senior Manager, Performance and Quality, you'll lead proposal development and formal client responses for the account, and coordinate the team's responses to client, external, and government audits. You'll turn complex contract, pricing, performance guarantee, and operational requirements into accurate, persuasive, on-time submissions. Every commitment and audit response you produce is supported, traceable, and clear to the client. In Finance and Contract Compliance, you'll link what proposals promise to how performance and quality are checked through audits and corrective action. You will also project-manage implementations and changes on the account.

**Primary responsibilities**
----------------------------

* Develop proposal strategies and response plans for renewals, RFPs, RFIs, client-requested program and benefit-change proposals, and contract amendments that align with account objectives and client requirements.
* Manage the end-to-end development and submission of proposals and formal client responses, from requirement intake through final review and delivery.
* Partner with account, executive, Finance, Legal, Clinical, and Operations leadership to define key messages and value propositions, and confirm that pricing, performance guarantee, and contract commitments are accurate and approved before submission.
* Write clear, persuasive, client-ready narratives and executive communications about capabilities, program results, and positions, and represent the team in client meetings on proposals and deliverables.
* Lead project management for implementations and account changes, such as new programs, vendor transitions, and benefit or system changes. Build and manage project plans for these and for RFPs, renewals, contract amendments, client deliverables, and audit responses, with timelines, milestones, owners, and dependencies. Plan for compressed client turnaround times and escalate at-risk items early.
* Research client needs, program developments, and market and competitive trends to inform proposal strategy and client recommendations.
* Implement standardized templates, content libraries, style guides, and quality checklists for proposals and audit responses, and train contributors to use them.
* Support contract negotiations during RFPs and amendments by coordinating redlines and negotiating items with Legal and leadership, and documenting each decision to keep, trade, or drop an item, with its approver, so the rationale stays on record.
* Own the audit request log and coordinate intake, scoping, ownership, and evidence production for client, external, and government audits of the account, including third-party audits triggered by performance guarantee escalation provisions.
* Perform quality reviews of audit responses and evidence packages to confirm every part of the request is addressed, amounts reconcile, and the response is clear to an independent reviewer; coordinate secure submission and retain final versions.
* Maintain internal corrective action plans (CAPs) for known contract breaches, so completed fixes are documented before the client asks, and lead the response when the client invokes the contract's formal CAP process. Track audit findings, management responses, fixes, and closeout against contract timelines, and report recurring performance and quality themes to leadership.

**Key deliverables**
--------------------

* Proposal and client-response calendar, plus a project plan for each RFP, renewal, contract amendment, implementation, and major account change.
* Proposal strategies and response plans for renewals, RFPs, RFIs, and client-requested proposals.
* Standard content library, templates, style guide, and quality checklist.
* Commitment and negotiating-items log tying each commitment and redline decision to its approver and source.
* Audit request log, scope and ownership matrix, and evidence-package standards.
* Internal CAP register for known contract breaches, plus a findings, management-response, and corrective-action tracker and audit closeout packages.
* Leadership summaries of open proposals, implementation and change status, at-risk deliverables, and audit status.

***\*\*\*This is a remote role, but the ideal candidate will live in the Eastern Time Zone\*\*\****

**Minimum qualifications**

* 7+ years of work experience.
* Experience managing end-to-end proposal or RFP responses for complex healthcare or PBM clients.
* Experience planning, executing, and delivering across concurrent deadlines and owners.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and proposal content-management tools.

**Preferred qualifications**

* PBM, health plan, or government program experience, including implementations or vendor transitions.
* Experience coordinating audits, regulatory requests, or evidence-based client reviews.
* Experience validating pricing, performance guarantee, or contract commitments in proposals.
* Proposal management or project management certification.

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

**Pay Range**

The typical pay range for this role is:

$67,900.00 - $182,549.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.

**Great benefits for great people**

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

 
This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. Who is Swire Coca-Cola? We are a family-owned bottling company with a story spanning over two centuries. We are one of the largest bottlers of Coca-Cola in North America and distribute more than 50 beverage brands and flavors creating joy for our customers every day. Our 8,000+ driven employees work hard as part of a team that delivers refreshment to over 30 million consumers across 13 states. Begin a journey with us at Swire Coca-Cola and belong to a community of dedicated team members who think big and believe in winning together.
 
 
**Job Details:** 
**Job Level:** 7
 
 
**Why you’ll love working at Swire Coca-Cola:** 
Swire Coca-Cola is committed to providing balance to support you in all aspects of your life, both at work and beyond. We offer the benefits you need for physical, financial, and emotional well-being.
 
 

* Health coverage (3 medical options, dental and vision). 401(k) Retirement Plan w/company match
* Health Savings Accounts w/company match
* FREE virtual primary care, acute care and physical therapy
* FREE Employee Assistance Program
* Company paid (vacation, holidays, sick time, bereavement, jury duty, maternity/parental, disability leave and volunteer time)

In addition to health benefits, Swire Coca-Cola is proud to offer you opportunities where you help give back directly to the communities and causes you care about. Note: Enrollment in a Swire Medical Plan is required for some benefits.
 
 
What does a Sr. Quality Manager do at Swire Coca-Cola?
 
Lead the Manufacturing Quality discipline at a manufacturing plant level to ensure that plant is operating to the Coca-Cola KORE standards and that all products produced maintain the highest standards of consumer quality for brand integrity.
 
 
**Responsibilities:** 

* Develop, guide and measure the in-plant quality standards that must be met to manufacture products that meet all KO and industry standards for consumer consumption
* Hire, train, and mentor Quality Lab Technicians and Lab/Sanitation Supervisors at the plant level to ensure they are qualified to perform all the quality processes and procedures required to deliver quality product to consumers
* Guide the creation and maintenance of documentation, processes, and procedures to fully comply with all KO KORE standards requirements, as well as any other industry/regulatory requirements for quality in manufacturing at the plant level
* Establish and maintain strong associations with other Coca-Cola bottlers in the Quality Management space in order to effectively learn best practices, provide guidance/counsel where appropriate, and be aware of changing trends and requirements that must be implemented at the plants
* Proactively develop relationships with local and state government agencies responsible for managing water usage and quality standards, discharge standards, etc
* Performs other duties as assigned

**Requirements:** 

* High School Diploma (or GED) required and
* College degree preferred in chemistry, biology, preferred or related science field
* 4+ years' experience in Quality Management in a food manufacturing industry – soft drink preferred
* Strong understanding of the science of soft drink production at the base molecular level
* Strong knowledge of industry quality standards for manufacturing of food grade products
* Specific knowledge of all state and local standards and requirements for water quality and raw materials for food grade production
* KO KORE and ISO quality standards in a soft drink environment

Come and join our Sparkling team!

**Job Description:**

**Summary of Position****:**

The Senior Quality Manager of Flight Line Quality Control Management, and Execution of Helicopter Flight Line of an FAA part 21 approved Quality System. The Senior Manager, Quality Control of Flight Line will ensure compliance and safety, balanced with cost in alignment with operations to safely bring aircraft to pre-flight, ground test, and flight testing. Driving the finalization process to the delivery and acceptance intent on ZERO defect aircraft being presented to customers. Provide technical leadership, leaning on knowledge of FAA P21 requirements, AS9100, and aerospace knowledge. The Senior Quality Manager of Flight Line, will also focus on personnel management and development, ensuring competencies equal to the business and market requirements. The Senior Manager will have a Continuous Improvement approach to processes while executing to the business plan.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities****:**

* Safe and on time actions bringing Production Helicopters to Operation, Ground Run, Flights, Acceptance & Delivery to Customer
* Resource Management, deployment of resources, training and building out Competencies of resources to meet customer and market demand
* Ensure compliance of Quality System with all relevant, FAA guidelines, procedures and policies.
* Represents QC as the prime contact for customer delivery activities
* Proactive measures in the planning and execution of aircraft operations, customer Acceptance and Delivery activity
* Continuous Improvement: using methods like DMAIC, statistical analysis to understand and improve processes and contributing to the efficiency of the Flight Line Operation

**Qualifications for Position****:**

**A. Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aviation Management, or a related technical discipline

**B. Experience**

* 5+ years of management and Quality experience or Equivalent

**C. Competencies & Attributes**

The successful candidate will have a working knowledge of AS9100 QMS and FAA requirements. Experience in Lean/Six Sigma, and a demonstrated approach to the job is a must. Must be a Leader and Change Agent with sound fundamentals in Quality Principles in Aerospace and Continuous Improvement. This Leader must demonstrate the ability to engage with partners and shareholders to find solutions, in execution and process. The candidate mut also demonstrate the ability to engage with stakeholders at Executive levels, internally, and externally including customers from the commercial and defense sectors.

**D. Licensure/Certification**

* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt desired, Green belt required
* ASQ Certification highly desired
* FAA Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) License or verified military equivalent desired

**Primary Location:**

US - Philadelphia

role.description:
**New England Village**

**Position:** Senior Director of Quality, Compliance and Risk

**Location:** Pembroke, MA 02359 (on-site)

**Salary:** $105,000-$120,000 annually

**Position Summary**

New England Village is seeking an experienced Senior Director of Quality, Compliance & Risk to provide organization-wide leadership for quality management, regulatory compliance, risk management, accreditation readiness, policy governance, and continuous improvement.

This is a senior leadership role for a professional with substantial prior experience in quality management and regulatory compliance within a complex, highly regulated environment. The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience leading quality and/or compliance functions and building systems that translate regulatory requirements, organizational findings, data, and risk into measurable and sustainable improvement.

The Senior Director works across programs and support departments to promote consistent standards, effective monitoring, clear accountability, regulatory readiness, and continuous improvement. Department leaders remain responsible for the quality, compliance, and performance of their respective areas, while the Senior Director provides the organizational framework, oversight, consultation, analysis, and escalation necessary to support enterprise accountability.

The Senior Director serves as New England Village's designated Compliance Officer, directly supervises the Director of Program Improvements & Supports and the Director of Program Implementation & Practice, and serves as a member of the Senior Leadership Team.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead and continuously strengthen the organization's quality management framework, including the Quality Management Plan, performance indicators, monitoring systems, trend analysis, corrective action, and continuous improvement.
* Serve as the organization's Compliance Officer and lead the continued development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of a formal enterprise compliance program.
* Maintain organizational readiness for licensing, accreditation, regulatory reviews, audits, surveys, investigations, inspections, and other external reviews.
* Establish and oversee effective approaches to internal quality and compliance review, risk assessment, root-cause analysis, corrective action, monitoring, and verification that improvements are sustained.
* Develop and maintain an organizational approach to identifying, assessing, mitigating, monitoring, and escalating significant regulatory, service, health and safety, privacy, financial, operational, and organizational risks.
* Analyze incidents, complaints, investigations, audit findings, corrective actions, regulatory findings, performance measures, and other data to identify patterns, systemic concerns, recurring issues, and emerging risks
* Lead and support effective policy and procedure governance, ensuring regulatory and organizational requirements are translated into practical and sustainable operations.
* Ensure significant findings result in meaningful corrective and improvement actions, with assigned accountability, measurable outcomes, follow-up, and evidence of effectiveness.
* Provide leadership and professional development to functions responsible for quality assessment, compliance monitoring, program improvement, implementation support, training, and practice fidelity.
* Work collaboratively with program and support leaders while maintaining the independence and objectivity necessary to identify concerns, challenge practices, and escalate significant or unresolved risk.
* Monitor changes in applicable regulatory and funding requirements and coordinate appropriate changes to policies, procedures, systems, training, monitoring, and organizational practices.
* Provide clear analysis, reporting, and recommendations regarding significant quality, compliance, regulatory, and risk matters to senior and executive leadership and designated Board committees.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in human services, healthcare administration, quality management, compliance, public administration, or a related field required; master's degree preferred.
* Minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in human services, healthcare, behavioral health, Medicaid-funded services, or a comparable highly regulated environment, including at least five years with significant responsibility for quality management, regulatory compliance, risk management, accreditation, or related organizational assurance functions.
* At least three years of progressive leadership experience, preferably including supervision of managers, senior professionals, or multidisciplinary functions.
* Knowledge of Massachusetts DDS and MassHealth requirements, with direct experience in IDD or comparable Massachusetts human services strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading a quality and/or compliance function, with responsibility for activities such as regulatory monitoring, internal review or audit, corrective action, quality improvement, investigations, risk assessment, or accreditation/licensing readiness.
* Demonstrated experience developing and operating formal quality or compliance systems, including monitoring plans, audit/review processes, corrective-action systems, quality measures, risk tracking, policies and procedures, and reporting to senior leadership.
* Demonstrated experience preparing an organization for licensing, accreditation, regulatory audits, surveys, investigations, or external reviews, including responding to findings and monitoring corrective actions through resolution.
* Demonstrated ability to analyze quality, compliance, incident, and operational data; identify systemic or recurring issues; conduct or guide root-cause analysis; and translate findings into measurable improvement.
* Experience presenting significant quality, compliance, and risk findings and recommendations to executive leadership, Boards or Board committees, regulators, auditors, accreditation bodies, or other external reviewers.
* Advanced proficiency with Microsoft 365, including Excel, SharePoint, Microsoft Lists, Forms, and Teams, and experience using technology to improve monitoring, reporting, workflow, and accountability.
* Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in a related field.
* Direct professional experience supporting services regulated by Massachusetts DDS and/or MassHealth.
* Direct experience in IDD or comparable Massachusetts human services.
* Previous experience serving as a Compliance Officer or in a significant leadership role within a formal organizational compliance program.
* Experience developing or administering confidential reporting, complaint, investigation, and non-retaliation processes.
* Experience with CARF accreditation, Massachusetts DDS licensing, MassHealth audit readiness, or comparable accreditation and regulatory-review processes.
* Professional certification such as CPHQ, CHC, CCEP, Lean Six Sigma, PMP, or another relevant quality, compliance, risk, or improvement credential.
* Experience with Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate, or comparable technology used to support monitoring, workflow, reporting, and organizational accountability
